name: cut
description: Cut plane for clipping contact visualization. Shows only contacts on one side of a defined plane.

keywords.description: Enable cut plane on contact plot item
keywords.syntax: cut active on type plane surface on front on back off origin (<x>,<y>,<z>) normal (<nx>,<ny>,<nz>)
notes: Typically front=on back=off to view one half, or front=off back=on for the other.
Example: cut active on type plane surface on front on back off origin (0,0,0) normal (0,1,0)
Example: cut active on type plane surface on front off back on origin (0,0,0) normal (0,0,1)

Parameters: active: on | off — enable or disable the cut plane; type: plane — cut geometry type; surface: on | off — show the cut surface; front: on | off — show material in front of cut plane; back: on | off — show material behind cut plane; origin: (x,y,z) — a point on the cut plane; normal: (nx,ny,nz) — normal direction of the cut plane
keywords.name: cut active on

keywords.description: Disable cut plane, restoring full visualization
keywords.name: cut active off

notes: Cut plane syntax is identical across ball, contact, and wall item types.
IMPORTANT: cut parameters must be set via 'plot item modify', not inline in 'plot item create'. Create the item first, then modify to add the cut.

PFC3D 9.7: cut keywords DO parse inline at create time - 'plot item create <type> cut ?' enumerates active/back/front/surface/type, with type = none/octant/plane/wedge and front/surface booleans. The 'must use plot item modify' rule above was verified on PFC2D 7.00; on 9.7 both routes parse.
During creation: Cut cannot be inlined in 'item create'. First create the item, then use 'item modify' to add the cut plane.
On 'plot item modify': plot "<name>" item modify <id> cut active on type plane surface on front off back on origin (0,0,0) normal (0,1,0)
Legend: Cut plane legend sub-settings exported in datafile

examples.command: legend ... cut ... title active on size 44 family 'Arial' style normal color 'black' ... origin active off ... normal active off ... orientation active off
